source.title: Feature Superposition in Neural Networks: From Theory to Practice
source.authors: Dai Shi; Xiao-Yu Li; Andi Han; José Miguel Hernández-Lobato

page_placements.theme: Measurement sensitivity, identifiability and canonical feature identities

record.file_problem: none; full survey text is present
record.tranche_reason: The survey includes its own analytical toy-code examples that examine sparse feature recovery with overlapping directions and show polysemantic neuron responses without overlapping feature directions. It does not reproduce the original training procedure.
record.gate_note: Rows record the survey's own worked examples in Section 2.3. Results attributed to other studies are cited literature, not results of this survey, and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a survey. Its own content is hand-built analytical illustrations: Example 2.4, and the 45° rotation in Figure 2, which it adapts from Prieto et al. (2026). Every empirical result on trained networks bearing on V1–V6 is cited from other work. The constructions fix the encoder by hand, so they show what a code can do, not what networks learn. They therefore do not test V1's claim about stored features in small networks. The rotation is a definitional argument relevant to V3, not a measurement of how polysemanticity arises in any system. A case for T5 on V3 is borderline at best, because the argument is borrowed and contains no result.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors, as a survey, conclude that what can be recovered from superposed codes depends on the feature distribution, error tolerance and decoder class. They also conclude that recovery methods need explicit feature targets and causal or interventional evidence. Polysemantic neurons, high reconstruction scores or convincing latent labels do not by themselves establish above-width recoverable features or canonical units. They add that whether trained networks are actually in superposition remains open, since no packing degree has been measured for an intermediate layer.
record.recipe_differences: A survey that organizes prior theory and practice, with analytical worked examples; it does not use the original toy-model training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The worked recovery example varies with feature sparsity and decoder class.

fits_no_version.finding: For two Bernoulli(p) features in one dimension with an antipodal code, a ReLU decoder gives R²=1−p/(1−p)→1 as p→0. The best linear decoder is capped at R²=1/2 for every p. Whether a code counts as superposition therefore depends on the decoder class.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether a code counts as superposition, and its packing degree, depends on the decoder class: a low linear-probe score need not mean the feature is absent.

fits_no_version.finding: Rotating an orthogonal two-feature code by 45° makes every neuron respond to both features while the feature directions stay orthogonal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron-level polysemanticity is coordinate-dependent and not by itself evidence of overlapping feature directions (a definitional argument adapted from Prieto et al. 2026).

record.problems: The relevant examples are analytical constructions rather than trained networks, and the survey reports no new empirical training or evaluation results for the claim.
record.rows_left_out: Results attributed to cited papers were excluded throughout, as required; the survey itself reports no additional directly tested results on these versions.

untested.parts: All of it. Trained toy-model geometry, the sparsity transition and regular polytopes are reviewed only from Elhage et al. 2022, Scherlis et al. and Prieto et al.
All of it. The capacity and importance allocation is reviewed from Scherlis et al. and Elhage et al.
All empirical parts. Incidental polysemanticity is reviewed from Lecomte et al. 2024. The rotation argument is definitional.
All of it. The LLM evidence (sparse probing, SAEs, Liu et al. scaling) is cited.
All of it. Non-canonicity, seed instability, absorption and frozen-random controls are cited (Leask, Gerasimov, Chanin, Korznikov).
All of it. Circular and manifold features are cited (Engels 2025a, Gurnee 2026a, Bhalla 2026).

record.verdict_notes: This is a review with no new empirical or training results. The reader's 'tests/T2' classification and its V1/V3 labels rested on pedagogical constructions, not measurements of any system, so all labels are removed. Gate_note correctly excluded cited results. If the database wants to credit the survey's synthesis, it bears most directly on V5, which it presents as challenged by cited work (Leask et al. 2025; Korznikov et al. 2026). Those verdicts belong to the cited studies.

versions.untested_parts: The examples do not train networks, establish a general sparsity-dependent training transition, or test the prevalence of regular geometries. The antipodal code is not a nearly orthogonal arrangement.
The capacity-allocation and importance claims are reviewed from cited work, not tested by this survey.
The survey's construction shows polysemantic neuron responses after rotating orthogonal directions; it does not test the prevalence of other causes of polysemanticity in trained models.
LLM feature spreading and SAE recovery are discussed through cited studies, not tested by this survey.
SAE feature completeness, stability, and canonicity are discussed through cited studies, not tested by this survey.
The survey discusses one-dimensional atoms and multidimensional representations, but supplies no original test comparing feature dimensionalities.

rows.subject: antipodal encoder W = [1, −1]
rows.operation_detail: Analytically evaluates per-feature recovery for independent Bernoulli features using a ReLU decoder.
rows.value: R² = 1 − p/(1 − p); tends to 1 as p → 0, and reaches at least 1 − ε when p ≤ ε/(1 + ε)
rows.note: This is a hand-specified code, not a trained network. Its feature directions are antipodal rather than nearly orthogonal; it demonstrates recoverability for two features in one dimension under the stated nonlinear decoder.
rows.check: Hand-specified antipodal code (W=[1,−1]), not a trained network. It shows that recovery depends on the decoder, not that small networks store sparse features as nearly orthogonal directions, so it does not measure V1. The text itself says the example is a pedagogical check of Definitions 2.1–2.2.

rows.subject: antipodal encoder W = [1, −1]
rows.operation_detail: Analytically evaluates the best affine linear readout for the same code.
rows.note: Shows that the recovery result in this example depends on decoder class; it does not test learned toy-model geometry.
rows.check: This is the comparator readout (best linear R²=1/2) for the same hand-built code. It is an analytic property of linear decoders, not evidence about learned toy-model geometry. Labelling it 'partial' for V1 was unfounded.

rows.subject: two-feature orthogonal code rotated by 45°
rows.operation_detail: Constructs a rotated representation and compares neuron responses with feature-direction geometry.
rows.measure: Neuron responses and feature-direction inner product
rows.baseline: Unrotated dedicated code has one feature per neuron
rows.value: Each neuron responds to both features; the feature directions remain orthogonal, with inner product 0
rows.note: The construction illustrates polysemantic neuron responses without feature-direction overlap or pressure to represent more features than dimensions.
rows.check: This is a constructed 45° rotation of an orthogonal code, taken from Prieto et al. (2026). It is a definitional point that neuron polysemanticity depends on the coordinate system. It does not measure polysemanticity arising in any trained system without capacity pressure, so it is not a test result for V3.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: It organizes and assesses superposition research rather than reporting its own test of the listed claim versions.

tranche.reason: The survey reviews prior claim-bearing results. Its hand-specified decoder example does not test learned geometry, capacity-driven polysemanticity, or representations in trained models.

source_check.notes: The reported recovery scores concern a stipulated antipodal encoder and alternative decoders, not a trained network. Both rows appropriately have no claim-version links.
